transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I… I keep checking things at home. Outlets, locks, tools, even dust. I go back over them again and again, trying to fix or make sure they’re okay, and it takes up most of the day. I get exhausted, but I still don’t really feel sure enough to stop.
Are you checking these things because you're afraid something bad might happen if you don't?

Yeah… mostly. Even if I know I did it right, I get this thought that maybe I missed a loose wire and the house could burn down, or I left a nail somewhere and my wife could get hurt. I try not to think about it, but it just comes back.
Do you ever feel like you have to perform these checks in a specific way or a certain number of times to feel like you've done them correctly?
Not really a number, no. It’s more… I keep going back over the same things — outlets, locks, tools, dust — checking or fixing them again and again. I don’t feel done, even when I’m worn out.
Do you feel like you need to check these things in a particular order to feel okay about them?

Not really an order, no. I just… keep circling back to the same things — outlets, locks, tools, dust — checking or fixing them until I’m worn out. Even then I don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone.
Do you feel like these checks are helping to prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… I guess that’s what it feels like. Like if I keep checking the outlets, the locks, the tools, cleaning up dust and stuff, then maybe I’m stopping something from going wrong. But even after I do it over and over, I still don’t really feel sure.
Do you ever feel like you need to check something a certain number of times before you can stop?

Not a set number, no. I just keep going back to the same things… outlets, locks, tools, dust. I check or fix them again and again, and even when I’m worn out, it still doesn’t feel like enough to stop.
Do you have any thoughts or mental images that you feel compelled to repeat over and over?

Yeah… kind of. I get these thoughts that won’t leave me alone, like maybe I missed a loose wire and it’s going to burn the house down, or I left a nail somewhere and my wife could get hurt. I know I probably did it right, but the thought just comes back worse when I try to push it away.
Do you ever feel like you have to repeat certain words or phrases to yourself over and over?

Not really words or phrases, no. It’s more… I keep going back over things in the house — outlets, locks, tools, dust — checking and fixing them again and again. I spend most of the day on it sometimes, and even then I don’t feel sure.
Do you feel compelled to think about certain thoughts or ideas over and over, beyond just the thoughts about the things you're checking?

Yeah… mostly it’s those same kinds of thoughts. Like even if I know I did the work right, my mind keeps throwing it back at me — that I missed a loose wire and the house could burn, or I left a nail and my wife could get hurt. I try not to think about it, but it just comes back harder.
Do you feel like you have to think about anything else over and over, besides the thoughts about the things you're checking?
Not that I can think of. It’s mostly just those things… the checking stuff. I don’t really notice anything else like that.
Do you feel like you must repeat your checking behaviors in exactly the same way each time?

Not exactly the same way, I don’t think. It’s more that I keep going back to the same things — the outlets, locks, tools, dust — checking or fixing them again and again. I can spend most of the day doing that, and even then it doesn’t feel… settled enough to leave alone.
Do you feel like the things you check or fix need to be in a certain condition or state for you to feel okay about them?

Yeah… I guess so. I keep going back over the outlets, locks, tools, dust… trying to get them right, or safe, or clean enough. I spend most of the day doing it sometimes, and even then I still don’t really feel sure enough to leave it alone.
Do you feel like you have to think about or mentally repeat anything else over and over, beyond the thoughts about the things you're checking?

Yeah… sort of. Even after I know I did something right, I’ll get these thoughts that maybe I missed a loose wire and the house could burn down, or I left a nail somewhere and my wife could get hurt. I try not to think about it, but it just comes back.
Do you feel like you have to think about or mentally repeat anything else over and over that isn't related to the things you're checking?

Not really outside of that. It’s mostly the same ugly thoughts… like even if I know I did the job right, I keep thinking maybe I missed a wire and the house will burn, or I left a nail and my wife’ll get hurt. I try to push it away, but it comes back worse.
Do you feel like you have to think about or mentally repeat anything over and over to make yourself feel better or to prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of the checking. I go back over the outlets, the locks, my tools, dust… just fixing or checking them again and again. It eats up most of the day sometimes. I’m trying to feel like it’s okay to stop, but I usually still don’t feel sure.
Do you feel like you have to think about or mentally repeat anything over and over that isn't related to the things you're checking?
I don’t think so… not apart from that. It’s hard to separate, but I haven’t noticed anything else like that.

Do you feel like you have to think about or mentally repeat certain things over and over to make yourself feel better or to prevent something bad from happening, outside of the thoughts about the things you're checking?

No… not really outside of that. It’s mostly the same stuff I keep going back to — outlets, locks, tools, dust. I check or fix it again and again, and even then I don’t really feel sure enough to leave it alone.
Do you feel like you have any other thoughts or mental images that you feel compelled to think about over and over, outside of the thoughts about checking things?

Yeah… I guess there are some. Like even if I know I did something right, I’ll get this thought that maybe I missed a loose wire and the house could burn down, or I left a nail somewhere and my wife could get hurt. I try not to think about it, but it just comes back.
Do you feel like the things you check or fix need to be arranged or organized in a specific way for you to feel okay about them?
I’m not sure… not really in a specific way. It’s more that I need to feel like it’s safe or done right. Not like lined up or organized, I don’t think.
Do you feel like you must perform your checking behaviors in a very specific manner to feel like you've done them correctly?

Yeah… I guess I do it a certain way. I keep going back over the same outlets, locks, tools, and dust, checking and fixing them again and again. It eats up most of the day, and even when I’m worn out, I still don’t really feel sure enough to stop.
